title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
gist: Hippolyte Fofack argues gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world's top reserve asset, framing this as both a hedge against 'a rogue America' and evidence of a structural shift toward a multipolar monetary order driven by technological diffusion and dispersing economic power; this is a paywalled teaser excerpt, so the full argument beyond the opening is not available.

themes.theme: Gold displaces Treasuries as top reserve asset

insights.claim: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world's top reserve asset, a shift the author attributes to gold offering a solution to the challenges posed by 'a rogue America.'
insights.speaker: Hippolyte Fofack
insights.so_what: If gold has genuinely displaced Treasuries as the top global reserve asset, this signals declining central-bank confidence in the safety/reliability of US sovereign debt as a reserve instrument, with implications for Treasury demand and yields.
insights.quote: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world's top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America.

insights.claim: Central banks bought record amounts of gold last year, with the increase marking the fourth-largest annual expansion of gold reserves on record.
insights.speaker: Hippolyte Fofack
insights.so_what: A top-four historical gold-buying year by central banks is a concrete, trackable data point supporting continued strength in gold demand and prices from official-sector buying.
insights.locator: central banks are buying record amounts of it

insights.claim: The Dutch central bank decided to move much of its gold reserves out of the United States, explicitly citing 'geopolitical unrest' as the reason.
insights.speaker: Hippolyte Fofack
insights.so_what: A named, concrete instance of a G10 central bank repatriating gold from US custody over geopolitical risk is a leading indicator other reserve managers may be watching or following.
insights.locator: The Dutch central bank's decision to move much of its gold reserves

insights.claim: The renewed relevance of gold reflects broader structural forces -- rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power globally -- that are creating a more diversified international monetary system beyond dollar dominance.
insights.speaker: Hippolyte Fofack
insights.so_what: Frames gold's rise as part of a longer-term multipolar monetary reordering rather than a temporary flight-to-safety trade, suggesting sustained rather than cyclical gold demand.
insights.locator: its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion
